Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real DB and code paths, no VM ever provisions, no card ever charges). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST for the operating rules (never build in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, verification-by-screenshot discipline, etc). Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (see /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt), base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

CONTEXT — a long session just finished building a light theme for this whole dashboard (dark was the only mode before; light is new, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) and found/fixed a long tail of bugs across most pages. You are ONE of 4 parallel agents auditing the REMAINING, not-yet-checked pages for the same classes of bugs. COORDINATION: you may rebuild (./rebuild.sh) and restart the nxeon-v2-web service as needed for your own verification — just don't leave it down when you finish, and do NOT create git commits (the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together). Stay within your assigned pages/files (listed below) so you don't collide with the other 3 agents working the same tree concurrently.

YOUR PAGES: /dashboard/billing, /dashboard/invoices, /dashboard/affiliate, /dashboard/partner, /dashboard/team, /dashboard/feedback, /dashboard/whats-new. Find each one's page component (app/dashboard/<name>/page.tsx, which will import a components/nx/<Name>View.tsx or similar — grep to find it) and any sub-tabs/modals it opens (billing in particular likely has an "add card"/"add funds" modal flow — check those too).

THE BUG TAXONOMY TO CHECK FOR ON EVERY PAGE (all of these have been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session — you're checking whether the same mistakes exist on your assigned pages):
1. A literal hardcoded color (hex or rgba, e.g. `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`, `text-[#7f9ad0]`) used for something that should adapt between themes, instead of the theme's own `--color-*` tokens / `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`, etc. (grep app/globals.css for the full token list). On the light page these often render as either invisible-on-invisible or a jarring leftover dark box.
2. A hero/banner section with its own fixed dark background + `text-white` heading — if it's not wrapped in the `.nx-dark-island` CSS class (also in app/globals.css), light mode's generic fix flips `text-white` to dark ink, making it invisible against a scrim that stayed dark on purpose. Look for `<header>` or hero `<div>`s with a literal dark gradient background.
3. `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) used to mean "always paint this literally white" (e.g. a toggle switch knob, an active-segment pill) — this breaks because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode. Fix: literal `bg-[#fff]` if it must always be bright regardless of theme, or a proper light-mode-aware treatment otherwise.
4. An `Icon` component (components/nx/Icon.tsx) rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored/gradient badge that has an intended contrasting text color set on the wrapper — the icon overrides that intended color with its own default tone class instead of inheriting it. Fix: pass `tone="inherit"`.
5. `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) sitting on something that is NOT actually a light-mode-adapted surface (e.g. its own literal-color decorative card) — gets wrongly retargeted by the global opacity-decoupling rule meant for text sitting on the actual page background.
6. Any canvas/backdrop using `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` or CSS `mix-blend-screen`/`mix-blend-lighten` — these only ever add light and wash to grey on a light page. If you find one NOT already using components/nx/auroraTheme.ts's `isLightTheme()`/`auroraComposite()`/`auroraStrandGradient()` helpers, wire it in (read components/nx/DomainsAurora.tsx as a working example of the pattern) rather than reinventing the fix.
7. A `.card-on`-style "selected" state, or any custom selected/active-state styling, that renders as a solid dark block regardless of theme — should look intentional (accent border/glow) rather than like a hole punched in an otherwise light page.
8. Genuine FUNCTIONAL bugs unrelated to theming — broken layout, a button that does nothing, a modal that doesn't close, text that's cut off, a state that never updates, real money-math looking wrong (this is a billing area — if something looks numerically off, check the underlying calculation, don't just restyle it) — note and fix anything you notice, not just color bugs.

WORKFLOW: for each page, log in via a Playwright script (must live under /opt/nxeon-v2/scripts/ per CLAUDE.md, e.g. scripts/_audit_b.mjs — delete it when you're done, this repo's convention is not to leave one-off scripts lying around), screenshot in BOTH dark (default) and light mode (`localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light'); document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating, same trick used everywhere else this session), actually LOOK at the screenshots (read them back as images), diagnose anything that looks wrong using the taxonomy above, fix it in the source, rebuild, re-screenshot to confirm the fix, then move to the next page. Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after every batch of edits.

Don't invent problems that aren't there — several pages may already be fine (if a page already uses `.card`/`.card-glass`/tokens throughout, it likely needs nothing). Only fix what's actually visibly or functionally broken. Write a final report listing every bug found (with a short description and the file it was in) and every fix made, plus any page you found to already be correct.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. /**
 * Post-login redirect validation.
 *
 * WHY ITS OWN FILE. This lived briefly in lib/actions.ts, which carries
 * `"use server"` — and in such a file EVERY export becomes a network-callable
 * server action, so a synchronous helper does not even compile ("Server Actions
 * must be async functions"). That constraint is not a formality: the same
 * property once turned `verifyTotpForUser` into a public 2FA brute-force oracle
 * simply by living in the wrong file, which is why lib/totp-verify.ts exists too.
 * A pure predicate belongs in a plain module.
 *
 * Note the compiler caught this only at `next build`; `tsc --noEmit` was clean.
 */
/**
 * A post-login destination that is guaranteed to be on this site, or null.
 *
 * An unvalidated `?next=` on a login form is an open redirect, which is a
 * phishing primitive: an attacker sends `…/login?next=https://evil.test/`, the
 * victim signs in on the REAL site and is handed to the attacker's page, already
 * primed to trust it. So this allows exactly one shape — a single-slash absolute
 * path — and discards everything else rather than trying to sanitise it:
 *
 *   "/dashboard/migrate"  -> kept
 *   "//evil.test/x"       -> rejected (protocol-relative; the browser treats it
 *                            as a host, and `startsWith("/")` alone lets it past)
 *   "https://evil.test"   -> rejected
 *   "/\\evil.test"        -> rejected (backslash is a slash to some parsers)
 *   "dashboard"           -> rejected (relative)
 */
export function safeNext(raw: FormDataEntryValue | null): string | null {
  const s = typeof raw === "string" ? raw.trim() : "";
  if (!s || s.length > 512) return null;
  if (!s.startsWith("/")) return null;
  if (s.startsWith("//") || s.startsWith("/\\")) return null;
  if (/[\x00-\x1f]/.test(s)) return null;
  return s;
}

/**
 * The single definition of "the same email address".
 *
 * `User.email` is `@unique` in Postgres, and a Postgres unique index is
 * CASE-SENSITIVE. Register and login stored and queried the address exactly as
 * it was typed, while `requestPasswordReset` lowercased it first. So a customer
 * who signed up as `Alice@Example.com` — which is what a phone keyboard produces
 * unless you fight it, because it auto-capitalises the first letter of a field —
 * had an account row no reset lookup could ever find. The reset form still
 * answered "If an account exists for that email, a reset link is on its way",
 * because that non-enumerating reply is correct and must stay. The result was a
 * customer locked out of their own account with no error, no email, and nothing
 * on screen suggesting anything had gone wrong.
 *
 * The fix is not "lowercase it in three more places" — that is the shape that
 * caused the bug, and the fourth place would drift too. Every write and every
 * lookup of a user's address goes through this one function, so the stored form
 * and the queried form cannot disagree.
 *
 * Deliberately conservative: case folding and whitespace only.
 *   - The local part of an address is case-SENSITIVE per RFC 5321 §2.4, but no
 *     mail provider anyone actually uses honours that, and treating `Alice@` and
 *     `alice@` as two accounts is a lockout generator, not a feature.
 *   - We do NOT strip Gmail dots or `+tag` suffixes. Those are provider-specific
 *     conventions; canonicalising them would silently merge addresses a customer
 *     considers distinct, and would make two different people collide.
 *
 * Pure, dependency-free, and unit-tested in test/auth-email-identity.test.ts.

 * the caller's schema validation exactly as it should — this function validates
 * nothing and must never be mistaken for a validator.

export function sameEmail(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi

# ── skip the marketing site ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redesign does not touch marketing, but it is ~137 of the ~195 route files
# and most of the 254 static pages, so it dominates a build we now run by hand
# after every change.
#
# Next excludes any folder whose name starts with `_` from routing, so renaming
# the route group is all it takes. This is a SANDBOX-ONLY, TEMPORARY rename: the
# trap puts it back whatever happens — including a failed build or a Ctrl-C — so
# git never sees it and nothing different is ever merged to prod.
#
# Set NX_FULL=1 to build the whole site (do this before any staging/prod pass,
# where marketing MUST be built and exercised).
MK="app/(marketing)"
MK_OFF="app/_marketing_skipped"
restore() { [ -d "$MK_OFF" ] && mv "$MK_OFF" "$MK"; }
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${NX_FULL:-0}" != "1" ] && [ -d "$MK" ]; then
  echo "==> skipping the marketing site (NX_FULL=1 to include it)"
  mv "$MK" "$MK_OFF"
fi

echo "==> stopping the server (it reads .next; building under it breaks it)"
systemctl stop nxeon-v2-web

echo "==> building"
start=$(date +%s)
# Capped so a runaway build is killed rather than squeezing the customer VMs,
# and niced so it always yields to them.
if systemd-run --scope --quiet --unit=v2-rebuild \
     -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p CPUWeight=30 \
     bash -c 'cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && export NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && npm run build' \
     > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
  echo "==> built in $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
else
  echo "!!! BUILD FAILED — the server is NOT being restarted on a broken build."
  echo "    Last 20 lines of $LOG:"
  tail -20 "$LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> starting"
systemctl start nxeon-v2-web
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 http://127.0.0.1:3021/login || true)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "==> up: /login $code"; exit 0; }
  sleep 2
done
echo "!!! server did not come up — check: journalctl -u nxeon-v2-web -n 40"
exit 1
